subject: math.CV
name: Cauchy integral theorem
statement: If f is holomorphic on a simply connected open subset Ω of ℂ, then its integral along every closed piecewise C¹ curve in Ω is zero.

subject: math.CV
name: Cauchy integral formula
statement: If f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of a closed disk and z lies inside its positively oriented boundary γ, then f(z) = (1/(2πi)) ∮γ f(ζ)/(ζ−z) dζ.

subject: math.CV
name: Cauchy derivative estimates
statement: If f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z−a| ≤ R and |f| ≤ M there, then |f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)| ≤ n!M/Rⁿ for every nonnegative integer n.

subject: math.CV
name: Liouville's theorem
statement: Every bounded entire function on ℂ is constant.

subject: math.CV
name: Fundamental theorem of algebra
statement: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root. Consequently, a polynomial of degree n has exactly n complex roots counted with multiplicity.

subject: math.CV
name: Identity theorem
statement: If two holomorphic functions on a connected open set agree on a set with an accumulation point inside that open set, they agree everywhere on it.

subject: math.CV
name: Maximum modulus principle
statement: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected open set cannot attain a local maximum of its modulus at an interior point.

subject: math.CV
name: Open mapping theorem for holomorphic functions
statement: Every nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected open subset of ℂ maps open subsets to open subsets of ℂ.

subject: math.CV
name: Schwarz's lemma
statement: If f is holomorphic on the unit disk, |f(z)| ≤ 1, and f(0) = 0, then |f(z)| ≤ |z| and |f′(0)| ≤ 1. Equality at a nonzero point, or |f′(0)| = 1, forces f(z) = eⁱᶿz for a real θ.

subject: math.CV
name: Rouché's theorem
statement: Let f and g be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closure of a bounded Jordan domain with piecewise smooth boundary. If |g| < |f| on the boundary, f and f+g have the same number of zeros in the domain, counted with multiplicity.

subject: math.CV
name: Argument principle
statement: If f is meromorphic near the closure of a bounded Jordan domain with piecewise smooth positively oriented boundary γ, with no zeros or poles on γ, then (1/(2πi)) ∮γ f′/f = N−P. Here N and P count the zeros and poles inside, with multiplicity.

subject: math.CV
name: Residue theorem
statement: If f is meromorphic near the closure of a bounded Jordan domain with piecewise smooth positively oriented boundary γ and has no poles on γ, then ∮γ f(z) dz = 2πi times the sum of its residues at the poles inside.

subject: math.CV
name: Morera's theorem
statement: If f is continuous on an open set Ω and its integral around the boundary of every triangle whose filled interior lies in Ω is zero, then f is holomorphic on Ω.

subject: math.CV
name: Weierstrass convergence theorem
statement: A sequence of holomorphic functions on Ω that converges uniformly on every compact subset has a holomorphic limit. Its derivatives of every order converge uniformly on compact subsets to the corresponding derivatives of that limit.

subject: math.CV
name: Hurwitz's theorem
statement: If zero-free holomorphic functions on a connected open set converge uniformly on compact subsets to f, then f is either zero-free or identically zero.

subject: math.CV
name: Montel's theorem
statement: Every locally uniformly bounded family of holomorphic functions on an open subset of ℂ is a normal family: every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function.

subject: math.CV
name: Riemann mapping theorem
statement: Every nonempty simply connected open subset of ℂ other than ℂ itself is biholomorphically equivalent to the unit disk.

subject: math.CV
name: Mittag–Leffler theorem
statement: For a closed discrete subset of an open set Ω ⊆ ℂ, with no accumulation point in Ω, and a prescribed finite principal part at each point, there is a meromorphic function on Ω with exactly those principal parts and no other poles.

subject: math.CV
name: Weierstrass factorization theorem
statement: Every nonzero entire function can be written as zᵐeᵍ⁽ᶻ⁾ times a convergent canonical product over its nonzero zeros, counted with multiplicity, where g is entire. The factors have the form Eₚ(w) = (1−w) exp(w + ⋯ + wᵖ/p), with E₀(w) = 1−w and suitable nonnegative integers p.

subject: math.CV
name: Great Picard theorem
statement: Near an isolated essential singularity, a holomorphic function takes every complex value, with at most one exception, infinitely often in every punctured neighborhood.
